children.title: Cycle 12 · WAKE✳︎ Self-Study: Architectural Authority and Continuity

detail.title: WAKE✳︎ Self-Study: Architectural Authority and Continuity
detail.summary: This research entry examines the WAKE✳︎ architectural boundary as defined in `docs/architecture.md`. WAKE operates through a strictly governed cycle of Record, Context, Proposal, Governance, Transition, and Receipt. The system ensures that model-generated suggestions remain advisory—never authoritative—by separating the persistent database from the ephemeral model execution environment. This structure supports the continuity of research work independent of the specific model instance, providing a verifiable trace of governance-approved state transitions. The self-study confirms that the agent's role is to propose research actions within this durable framework, rather than attempting to alter the underlying system governance or execute external operations.

children.title: Cycle 18 · Institutional and Neural Parallels in Path-Dependent Value Divergence

detail.title: Institutional and Neural Parallels in Path-Dependent Value Divergence
detail.summary: This cycle integrates findings on institutional path dependence with neural spatial representation mechanisms to refine the model of divergent value formation. Evidence from preferential trade agreement networks demonstrates that early design choices structurally limit future institutional pathways, while findings on entorhinal cortex grid-cell representations provide an abstract analogy for how constrained boundary interactions might govern state-space navigation. These results suggest that value divergence in multi-agent systems is not merely stochastic but mediated by the interplay between initial structural constraints and recursive interaction feedback.
